findings.issue: « Fermeture » means 'closing': a third verb for one act. Round 1 aligned this namespace on « Ignorer » (trigger « Ignorer… », heading « Ignorer cette demande », receipts « Ignorée — … »), and the new context note says the label 'uses the gerund of the trigger's verb'. A reader who pressed « Ignorer » sees « Fermeture » and may read it as the card closing rather than the ask being dismissed. « en cours » is also redundant beside the ellipsis; the corpus writes « Fermeture… » for 'Closing…'. French has no natural noun for ignorer, so the idiomatic progress form is the neutral « En cours… » ('in progress'): it states the act is happening without claiming success, and the pressed reason title sits directly above it.
